observations: Industrial sewing machine on a white table with a treadle pedal.
The machine head has a red oval logo with 'Emel' in white text.
A model plate is visible on the right side of the head, but the text is too blurry to read.
The machine is equipped with a bobbin winder and a thread stand.
The table has a built-in power switch and a ruler on the edge.
The machine shows some surface dust and minor wear.

claims.evidence: photo 0 and photo 1 show the Emel logo on the machine head.
The photos show the machine is dusty and used, but internal mechanical condition is unknown.
No photo shows this clearly enough to read.

claims.claim: the motor runs smooth. All accessories and the original manual, never serviced because nothing ever went wrong.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The machine may not sew or may have internal mechanical faults.
risks.proof: A video of the machine sewing through fabric.

risks.risk: The motor may be weak, noisy, or burnt.
risks.proof: A video of the motor running at full speed.

risks.risk: The treadle pedal may be broken or the foot control not working.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine running while the pedal is being used.

risks.risk: The machine may be a generic brand rather than the specific Emel model claimed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model plate on the machine head.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic industrial sewing machine

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the machine sewing a piece of fabric to demonstrate it works.
Video of the motor running to check for noise or overheating.
Video of the treadle pedal being used to operate the machine.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
